cues.zh: 加热是氧化脂肪的好办法，而植物油在进入厨房之前早就被反复加热过了。

cues.en: There are many steps to create edible oil and several of them involve very high heat.
cues.zh: 制作食用油要经过许多步骤，其中好几步都涉及非常高的温度。

cues.en: The oil is heated to 80 degrees Celsius during the acid wash process.

cues.zh: 在中和过程中，油温最高能达到95摄氏度。

cues.en: The bleaching earth step is carried out between ninety and one hundred and ten degrees centigrade for thirty minutes. At this point, the oil has oxidized so much that it's rancid and would taste terrible and smell awful if you ate it as is.
cues.zh: 漂白土处理步骤在90到110摄氏度之间进行，持续30分钟。此时，油已经氧化得非常严重，已经酸败，如果直接食用，味道会很糟糕，气味也很难闻。

cues.zh: 除臭

cues.zh: 处理。

cues.zh: 在这一 extensive 脱臭过程中，油会再次被加热，温度可高达260度。

cues.en: Heat isn't the only way to oxidize vegetable oils. They can oxidize just sitting on the shelf. Walnut oil, for example, which has plenty of linoleic acid,
cues.zh: 热量并不是让植物油氧化的唯一方式。就算只是放在架子上，它们也会氧化。比如核桃油，它含有大量亚油酸，

cues.zh: 仅仅在储存中放着，几天之内就会很容易地氧化，就像你在这里看到的这样。

cues.en: Vegetable oils also oxidize while sitting in your body creating toxic oxidation products like an aldehyde called four h n e.
cues.zh: 植物油还会在你的体内氧化，产生有毒的氧化产物，比如一种叫 4-HNE 的醛类物质。

cues.en: Four h n e is actually considered to be the most toxic aldehyde and this compound has been associated with aging, heart disease, diabetes, and Alzheimer's.
cues.zh: 4-HNE 实际上被认为是毒性最强的醛类，这种化合物与衰老、心脏病、糖尿病和阿尔茨海默病都有关联。

cues.en: Neuroscientist Tetsumori Yamashima
cues.zh: 神经科学家 Tetsumori Yamashima

cues.en: has done plenty of research on vegetable oils and four h n e. He's published multiple papers on the damaging effects of this compound and why people need to avoid vegetable oils because they oxidize into four h n e in our bodies.
cues.zh: 对植物油和 4-HNE 做了大量研究。他发表了多篇论文，探讨这种化合物的危害，以及人们为什么需要避开植物油，因为植物油会在我们体内氧化成 4-HNE。

cues.en: This book of his is titled stop eating vegetable oils to save your brain and blood vessels.
cues.zh: 他的这本著作名叫《别吃植物油，拯救你的大脑和血管》。

cues.en: He's even gone as far as to say that the real culprit behind Alzheimer's
cues.zh: 他甚至直言，阿尔茨海默

cues.en: Do you ever feel more tired than you should be? Like, you're just low on energy and can't concentrate for seemingly no reason, and you're thinking, is it normal to require this much coffee just to muster the energy to function?
cues.zh: 你有没有觉得自己累得不太正常？就是能量很低、似乎无缘无故无法集中注意力，然后心想：需要这么多咖啡才能勉强打起精神运转，这正常吗？

cues.en: But what is energy when you're talking about the body?
cues.zh: 但说到身体时，能量到底是什么？

cues.en: Here's a pop quiz. What do breathing, food, cyanide, and Star Wars all have in common?
cues.zh: 来个小测验。呼吸、食物、氰化物和《星球大战》有什么共同点？

cues.en: Midichlorians,
cues.zh: 米迪原虫，

cues.en: microscopic life forms live in the cells of living things that determine your propensity
cues.zh: 是生活在生物细胞中的微型生命体，决定你

cues.en: to use the force.
cues.zh: 使用原力的倾向。

cues.en: Actually, no. But midichlorians are obviously based off of mitochondria.
cues.zh: 其实不是。但米迪原虫显然是以线粒体为原型的。

cues.en: Mitochondria are found in nearly all cells in the human body.
cues.zh: 人体几乎所有细胞中都有线粒体。

cues.en: They are the powerhouse of the cell and the reason you breathe and eat food.
cues.zh: 它们是细胞的能量工厂，也是你呼吸和进食的原因。

cues.en: Mitochondria use food calories and oxygen to create energy in the form of a compound called ATP.
cues.zh: 线粒体利用食物中的热量和氧气，生成一种名为 ATP 的化合物，以此产生能量。

cues.en: We are incredibly reliant on our mitochondria to smoothly and efficiently produce massive amounts of energy.
cues.zh: 我们极其依赖线粒体平稳高效地产生大量能量。

cues.en: We need so much energy that if you took all the molecules of ATP you made in a day and put it on the scale, it would weigh as much as you.
cues.zh: 我们需要的能量如此之多，如果把一天产生的所有 ATP 分子放到秤上，重量会和你一样。

cues.en: We make our body weight in ATP
cues.zh: 我们产生的 ATP 重量相当于自己的体重

cues.en: every day.
cues.zh: 每一天。

cues.en: If you messed up this energy supply,
cues.zh: 如果这个能量供应出了问题，

cues.en: things would go haywire rapidly.
cues.zh: 事情会迅速失控。

cues.en: This is how cyanide kills people so quickly. It damages the mitochondria's
cues.zh: 这就是氰化物能如此迅速致人死亡的原因。它会损害线粒体

cues.en: ability to make energy.
cues.zh: 产生能量的能力。

cues.en: Un surprisingly,
cues.zh: 不出所料，

cues.en: some instances of feelings of excessively low energy or fatigue
cues.zh: 有些极度低能量或疲劳感的情况

cues.en: have been linked to poor mitochondrial function.
cues.zh: 已被发现与线粒体功能不佳有关。

cues.en: Evolutionary biologist doctor Douglas c Wallace is arguing here that medicine focuses too much on anatomy
cues.zh: 进化生物学家道格拉斯·C·华莱士博士在这里主张，医学过于关注解剖结构

cues.en: and not enough on animation.
cues.zh: 而对“生命活动”关注不足。

cues.en: That is the energy production necessary to animate the anatomy.
cues.zh: 也就是让解剖结构动起来所需的能量生产。

cues.en: Scientists are starting to see that mitochondrial
cues.zh: 科学家们开始认识到，线粒体

cues.en: dysfunction
cues.zh: 功能障碍

cues.en: may play a central role in the development of many diseases, including heart disease and Alzheimer's.
cues.zh: 可能在许多疾病的发展中发挥核心作用，包括心脏病和阿尔茨海默病。

cues.en: That's not all that surprising because the heart and brain require massive amounts of energy to work properly.
cues.zh: 这并不太令人意外，因为心脏和大脑需要大量能量才能正常运作。

cues.en: It's also well known that the mitochondria are dysfunctional in obesity and diabetes.
cues.zh: 同样众所周知的是，线粒体在肥胖和糖尿病中会出现功能障碍。

cues.en: In fact, the world's most prescribed diabetes drug metformin,
cues.zh: 事实上，全球处方量最大的糖尿病药物二甲双胍，

cues.en: which is one of the few that also helps patients lose weight, acts on the mitochondria.
cues.zh: 也是少数能帮助患者减重的药物之一，作用于线粒体。

cues.en: Okay. But where does vegetable oil come into play in all of this?
cues.zh: 好。但植物油在这其中又扮演什么角色呢？

cues.en: Well, surprise surprise, vegetable oils can damage the mitochondria.
cues.zh: 嗯，不出所料，植物油会损害线粒体。

cues.en: To make this real simple, you can think of the mitochondria's energy production as a conveyor belt at a factory that's pumping out ATP energy.
cues.zh: 简单来说，你可以把线粒体的能量生产想象成工厂里一条不断产出ATP能量的传送带。

cues.en: After your body pulls electrons from the food you eat, complexes and electron transporters pass electrons down this conveyor belt,
cues.zh: 你的身体从食物中提取电子后，复合物和电子转运体让电子沿着这条传送带向下传递，

cues.en: the inner membrane of the mitochondria.
cues.zh: 也就是线粒体内膜。

cues.en: This results in protons being pumped up here and then the protons get sucked into this ATP synthesis enzyme to make ATP.
cues.zh: 这导致质子被泵到这里，然后质子被吸入这个ATP合成酶来制造ATP。

cues.en: Now the conveyor belt, the inner membrane, has plenty of something called cardiolipin.
cues.zh: 这条传送带，也就是内膜，含有大量一种叫做心磷脂的物质。

cues.en: This is important because this is what's damaged when you consume plenty of vegetable oils.
cues.zh: 这很重要，因为当你摄入大量植物油时，受损的正是这个。

cues.en: When the linoleic acid from vegetable oils accumulates in your body, you can get what's called a peroxidation
cues.zh: 当植物油中的亚油酸在体内积累时，会发生所谓的过氧化

cues.en: cascade,
cues.zh: 级联反应，

cues.en: where kind of like dominoes,
cues.zh: 就像多米诺骨牌一样，

cues.en: one molecule of linoleic acid oxidizes
cues.zh: 一个亚油酸分子被氧化，

cues.en: and produces a substance that can oxidize another molecule of linoleic acid, and that produces more of that substance that can go on and damage another molecule of linoleic acid and so on and so on. It's a chain reaction.
cues.zh: 产生一种能氧化另一个亚油酸分子的物质，进而产生更多这种物质，继续去破坏下一个亚油酸分子，如此循环往复。这就是链式反应。

cues.en: This chain reaction can go on to affect the cardiolipin
cues.zh: 这种链式反应会继续影响心磷脂，

cues.en: in your mitochondria.
cues.zh: 也就是你线粒体里的心磷脂。

cues.en: As this study shows here, when rats eat a linoleic acid rich vegetable oil diet,
cues.zh: 正如这项研究所示，当大鼠食用富含亚油酸的植物油饮食时，

cues.en: markers of oxidized fat doubled.
cues.zh: 氧化脂肪的标志物翻了一倍。

cues.en: And in the heart, the content of cardiolipin,
cues.zh: 而在心脏中，心磷脂的含量，

cues.en: the stuff your mitochondria needs to properly produce energy,
cues.zh: 也就是线粒体正常产能所需的物质，

cues.en: was reduced fivefold.
cues.zh: 减少了五倍。

cues.en: In this study, the cardiolipin of diabetic and nondiabetic
cues.zh: 在这项研究中，糖尿病和非糖尿病

cues.en: rats reduced drastically when they were fed a vegetable oil diet,
cues.zh: 大鼠的心磷脂在喂食植物油饮食后急剧减少，

cues.en: and the mitochondria of the vegetable oil fed diabetic rats completely collapsed
cues.zh: 而喂食植物油的糖尿病大鼠的线粒体完全崩溃，

cues.en: into these crumpled blobs.
cues.zh: 变成了这些皱缩的团块。

cues.en: Even the textbook, recent advances in mitochondrial medicine,
cues.zh: 甚至连教科书《线粒体医学新进展》

cues.en: acknowledges that omega six fatty acids like those found in vegetable oil may damage various organs including the pancreas,
cues.zh: 也承认，植物油中的这类欧米伽6脂肪酸可能损害包括胰腺在内的多个器官，

cues.en: which would worsen metabolic syndrome
cues.zh: 这会加重代谢综合征

cues.en: and type two diabetes.
cues.zh: 和二型糖尿病。

cues.en: So going back to the first study, what happened to the normal rats whose mitochondrial cardiolipin
cues.zh: 那么回到第一项研究，那些因食用植物油而导致线粒体心磷脂

cues.en: was reduced so much from eating vegetable oils?
cues.zh: 大幅减少的正常大鼠，后来怎么样了？

cues.en: In just four weeks, these rats had heart failure.
cues.zh: 仅仅四周，这些大鼠就出现了心力衰竭。

cues.en: Developing heart failure that fast is very alarming, but, of course, humans are not rats, so it's not like eating a bunch of mayonnaise will give you heart failure in a couple weeks. It's going to take a very long time of consuming plenty of vegetable oil for damage to become apparent.
cues.zh: 这么快发生心力衰竭非常令人警觉，但当然，人不是大鼠，所以并不是吃一堆蛋黄酱就会在几周内得心力衰竭。要摄入大量植物油很长时间，损害才会显现。

cues.en: But how long? Well, let me mention one last study. The 1969
cues.zh: 但需要多久？让我再提最后一项研究。1969年的

cues.en: LA Veterans Administration
cues.zh: LA Veterans Administration

cues.en: Hospital study, another very well controlled clinical diet trial where people 60
cues.zh: 医院研究，另一项控制得非常好的临床饮食试验，受试者是60

cues.en: were given either animal fats or vegetable oils.
cues.zh: 分别给予动物脂肪或植物油。

cues.en: To cut to the chase, the people in the vegetable oil group were dying more. And this was the case even though there were twice as many heavy smokers in the animal fat group.
cues.zh: 直接说结果，植物油组的人死亡更多。而且即使动物脂肪组里重度吸烟者人数是两倍，情况依然如此。

cues.en: The interesting part is that this study was so long, eight years,
cues.zh: 有意思的是，这项研究持续了很长时间，八年，

cues.en: and it took many years to clearly see the negative effect of the vegetable oil diet.
cues.zh: 而且花了很多年才清楚看到植物油饮食的负面影响。

cues.en: The study authors concluded that to truly understand the negative health effect of vegetable oils,
cues.zh: 研究作者得出结论，要真正理解植物油对健康的负面影响，

cues.en: maybe studies need to be much longer than eight years,
cues.zh: 也许研究需要比八年长得多，

cues.en: but most only last five years at best.
cues.zh: 但大多数研究最多只持续五年。

cues.en: So to sum all this up, vegetable oils which are rich in the polyunsaturated omega six fat linoleic acid displace saturated fats which we had been eating for thousands of years.
cues.zh: 总结一下，富含多不饱和 omega-6 脂肪亚油酸的植物油，取代了我们几千年来一直吃的饱和脂肪。

cues.en: The consumption of these new oils
cues.zh: 这些新油的消费

cues.en: happen to correlate with rates of obesity, diabetes, and Alzheimer's.
cues.zh: 恰好与肥胖、糖尿病和阿尔茨海默病的发病率相关。

cues.en: Correlations are just correlations, but it's well known that polyunsaturated
cues.zh: 相关性只是相关性，但众所周知，多不饱和

cues.en: fats oxidize very easily creating oxidation products which are toxic to humans.
cues.zh: 脂肪极易氧化，产生对人体有毒的氧化产物。

cues.en: Not only that, but linoleic acid accumulates in the body where it can oxidize
cues.zh: 不仅如此，亚油酸还会在体内积累，并在那里氧化

cues.en: creating these harmful oxidation products
cues.zh: 产生这些有害的氧化产物

cues.en: and damaging our mitochondria.
cues.zh: 损害我们的线粒体。

cues.en: And lastly, well controlled
cues.zh: 最后，严格控制的

cues.en: trials have found worse outcomes for people on a vegetable oil diet.
cues.zh: 试验发现，采用植物油饮食的人结果更差。

cues.en: So something I've been thinking about is,
cues.zh: 所以我一直在思考的是，

cues.en: if this is such a big deal, why isn't it a bigger topic? Why aren't more people interested in vegetable oils the way people are interested in the health effects of say sugar?
cues.zh: 如果这如此重要，为什么它不是更大的话题？为什么没有更多人对植物油感兴趣，就像人们对糖的健康影响感兴趣那样？

cues.en: Well, I think the difference is sugar tastes and makes us feel great.
cues.zh: 嗯，我认为区别在于糖有味道，让我们感觉很棒。

cues.en: If you took it out of your food, you'd definitely notice.
cues.zh: 如果你把它从食物中去除，你肯定会注意到。

cues.en: So I think some people intuitively think, this has gotta be too good to be true. Maybe sugar is bad for me.
cues.zh: 所以我认为有些人直觉上会想，这好得不像真的。也许糖对我有害。

cues.en: But with vegetable oils, they're a lot like the sawdust in William Osmond's rice crispy treats. They're just there, hard to notice, hiding in your food.
cues.zh: 但植物油，它们很像威廉·奥斯蒙德米脆饼里的锯末。它们就在那里，很难注意到，藏在你的食物里。

cues.en: I mean, how often do you think about the fat used to make your food?
cues.zh: 我的意思是，你多久会想到用来制作食物的脂肪？

cues.en: If someone swapped the sugar in your coffee with stevia or Splenda,
cues.zh: 如果有人把你咖啡里的糖换成甜菊糖或善品糖，

cues.en: you'd notice pretty quickly.
cues.zh: 你很快就会注意到。

cues.en: But could you even tell if the aromatic vegetables you ordered at a restaurant were sauteed in canola oil instead of butter?
cues.zh: 但你能分辨出你在餐厅点的香炒蔬菜是用菜籽油而不是黄油炒的吗？

cues.en: Here's a quick quiz where the answer might surprise you.
cues.zh: 这里有一个快速测验，答案可能会让你惊讶。

cues.en: The greenhouse gases in the Earth's atmosphere absorb radiation
cues.zh: 地球大气中的温室气体会吸收辐射

cues.en: strongly in the infrared wavelengths.
cues.zh: 在红外波段吸收得特别强。

cues.en: When they absorb light, they heat up and eventually this heat is spread mostly through convection around the earth's surface.
cues.zh: 当它们吸收光线时，会升温，最终这些热量主要通过地表周围的对流散开。

cues.en: Warm objects like earth and the sun both emit heat in the form of infrared radiation.
cues.zh: 像地球和太阳这样温暖的物体，都会以红外辐射的形式散发热量。

cues.en: So is the greenhouse effect predominantly driven by infrared radiation emitted from the earth or the sun?
cues.zh: 那么，温室效应主要是由地球发出的红外辐射驱动，还是由太阳发出的红外辐射驱动？

cues.en: If you wanna know the answer, you'll have to check out Brilliant's physics of the everyday course.
cues.zh: 如果你想知道答案，得去看看 Brilliant 的“日常物理”课程。
